subject: Temporary keystore / ephemeral KMS exception - evidence & risk assessment
messages:
From: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@innohealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: sec@innohealth.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Evidence request: temporary keystore proxy / ephemeral KMS exception

Hi Karthik,

We hit a compliance checkpoint during our HIPAA readiness review and need a short-term carveout for one of our pilot tenants. During the pilot we used Redwood's ephemeral keystore proxy (ephemeral keys) and the auditor is asking for:

- evidence that the key material was generated and rotated as described;
- a verifiable audit trace of token/key usage for the tenant for a 30-day window; and
- an exception letter or attestation describing scope, retention, and access controls for the retained snapshot.

Our asks: can Redwood produce a scoped evidence bundle (logs + signed snapshot of the keystore metadata) limited to tenant ID: INH-7861, retention window 2026-08-01 -> 2026-08-31, and a short risk assessment for using a temporary retention bucket instead of full BYOK escrow?

If this is feasible, please let us know what you need from our side (POC, legal contact, list of tenant IDs, or any forms). We are on a tight window — audit kickoff 2026-09-20 and would appreciate confirmation by EOD Monday (2026-09-14).

Thanks,
Evelyn Shaw
Head of Security Operations
InnoHealth

[attachment: compliance_questionnaire.pdf (pdf)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@innohealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: temporary keystore proxy / ephemeral KMS exception

Evelyn — thanks for the clear ask and timeline. Looping in Ben (Security Ops), Marissa (Compliance), and Naomi (Product PM) so we can triage and give a firm plan.

Quick summary of what we heard: scoped evidence bundle for tenant INH-7861 for 2026-08-01 -> 2026-08-31, plus a short risk write-up and an exception/attestation. Target confirmation requested by EOD 2026-09-14 to hit your audit kickoff.

Immediate clarifying questions for InnoHealth:
1) Is the required retention only metadata + audit lines (key IDs, rotation events, request logs), or do you need ciphertext/key material escrow?
2) Any specific regulator/law we should cite in the attestation text (e.g., HIPAA section)?
3) Do you prefer a signed snapshot (WORM object with signed manifest) or a streamed export into a shared bucket?

Proposed next steps on our side: Ben, can you estimate the effort to extract a scoped audit bundle and produce a signed manifest? Naomi, can you confirm whether this requires moving the tenant to Dedicated for the evidence path or if a scoped export from hosted infra is acceptable? Marissa, will Legal/Compliance be able to draft an attestation template or do you want InnoHealth legal to propose language first?

If easier, we can do a short 30-min alignment call Monday morning (2026-09-14).

Thanks — Karthik
Principal Product Manager, Security Integrations
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: temporary keystore proxy / ephemeral KMS exception

Karthik / team — I looked up the INH-7861 tenant and the ephemeral keystore flow used during the pilot. A few technical notes and questions before we commit to an approach:

- The ephemeral keys we generate are not stored long-term; we only persist rotation metadata and request logs. If the customer is asking for ciphertext/key material, that will require a fundamentally different path (BYOK escrow or HSM export).
- What we can reasonably produce without changing runtime behavior: request logs (timestamp, operation, requester identity), keystore metadata (key ids, rotation events, TTLs), and a signed manifest proving the snapshot integrity.

Questions:
1) Confirm retention window and tenant list (Evelyn indicated 2026-08-01 -> 2026-08-31 for INH-7861).
2) Do they need per-request payload identifiers (token ids) included, or only key-level traces?
3) Will InnoHealth accept a scoped export stored in a locked S3 bucket with limited access for 90 days, or do they require a shorter/longer window?

I've attached a draft of the audit log schema we plan to use for the export. If approved, I estimate ~2 engineer-days to assemble the export + 1/2 day for the signed manifest process and documentation.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Security Operations
Redwood Inference

[attachment: audit_log_schema_v2.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: temporary keystore proxy / ephemeral KMS exception

Team — high-level Compliance perspective: temporary retention of ephemeral key metadata is feasible but high-touch. A few control points we must satisfy before we produce anything:

- Principle of least privilege: the export must be scoped strictly to INH-7861 and only the fields required by the auditor. No full key material exfiltration.
- Access governance: we need a single named reviewer from InnoHealth and a Redwood custodian with logged approvals; all access must be timeboxed.
- Legal language: we can provide an attestation describing the scoped snapshot and retention, but Legal asks for the customer to confirm that the snapshot will be used solely for the audit and not re-ingested.

I've attached a quick CSV with suggested retention window categories and recommended access durations. If the customer requires HSM-backed BYOK or long-term escrow, escalate to PrivOps/Enterprise for an amended engagement.

Marissa Cole
Head of Compliance
Redwood Inference

[attachment: retention_windows.csv (csv)]

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: temporary keystore proxy / ephemeral KMS exception

Thanks — good points all around. Proposed action plan (quick, 3 steps) and asks:

1) Scope export: Ben to produce scoped export containing request logs and keystore metadata for INH-7861 for Aug 2026 window. Export format per audit_log_schema_v2.pdf. (ETA: 2 eng days).
2) Snapshot & manifest: create a signed manifest (SHA256) for the export, store in a locked retention bucket with strictly limited ACLs. Redwood to provide a short attestation describing scope and access controls.
3) Legal/Attestation: Marissa to draft a 1-page attestation template we can sign and hand to InnoHealth.

Attachments: I prepared a short checklist to help keep the pack consistent if Ben/SEs produce more than one export. See attached: proposed_evidence_checklist.docx

Naomi — need product input: does this approach require any infra changes or a formal roadmap ticket (e.g., move to Dedicated for the tenant)? If it can be done from hosted infra without service-impact, I'd prefer the scoped export route to avoid long-term change.

Ben — please confirm ETA and whether the export requires a maintenance window. Marissa — please flag any legal stickiness and whether the attestation should reference any specific HIPAA clauses.

Karthik

[attachment: proposed_evidence_checklist.docx (docx)]

From: Evelyn Shaw <evelyn.shaw@innohealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: sec@innohealth.com
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 23:43:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: temporary keystore proxy / ephemeral KMS exception

Karthik / team — thank you, that plan looks acceptable in principle. A few confirmations from our side:

- Retention window confirmed: INH-7861, 2026-08-01 -> 2026-08-31. We only need metadata and request logs; no ciphertext or key material.
- Access: InnoHealth will provide a single named reviewer (legal contact: Claire Nunez) and agrees that the snapshot will be used strictly for audit purposes and then destroyed.
- Storage preference: shared S3 bucket with a signed manifest is fine; please mark the object as locked and provide ACL + access log evidence.

We appreciate the checklist. I've uploaded our standard audit questionnaire to a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bExampleDriveLink. I can join a 30-min alignment on 2026-09-16 14:00 UTC if that works for Ben/Marissa.

Evelyn
Head of Security Operations
InnoHealth
